summary: Ravalli County, MT lookout on Sula Peak: first built 1929, destroyed by wildfire in 2000, rebuilt 2001 as a two-story cab; listed standing; no access information found.

facts.design: Two-story octagonal cab (rebuilt 2001); earlier gable-roofed L-4 ground cab (1929) and 10-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab

events.note: Early gable-roofed L-4 ground cab; Missoula newspaper reported the new lookout almost finished in June 1929
10-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab, per Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com dates a similar tower to 1957 with a question mark
Tower legs enclosed with concrete blocks; newspaper item of February 1960 says the base was finished that fall
Staffed to 1996 per firelookout.com; staffed again in 1999
Destroyed by a wildfire (firelookout.com: forest fire; Forest Lookouts: wildfire)
New two-story octagonal lookout (firelookout.com); one-of-a-kind design (Forest Lookouts)

corrections.proposed: Two-story octagonal cab (2001); earlier L-4 cabs (1929, 1934)
corrections.why: L-4 describes the early cabs. The 2001 rebuild is a two-story octagonal lookout per firelookout.com.
The record starts at 2001 and omits the original 1929 lookout and the 2000 fire that the 2001 building replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives a 10-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab for 1934 (citing Kresek). Firelookout.com dates a similar tower to 1957, with a question mark. The story gives the 1934 date and notes the other.

notes_for_editor: Both pages read date the 2001 rebuild to 2001. One search summary (not read, not cited) pointed to a July 2002 Missoulian piece and a 2002 reopening; check before publishing if the date matters. Record height_m of 3.0 has no source in the pages read, so it is not corrected here; check the west_us_lookouts source. Access and rental: no information found, and the Bitterroot history page does not name Sula Peak. Current staffing is unknown; last known personnel are listed for 2002. Read budget: 4 cached page reads and 1 WebSearch.
